page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 10.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing approximately 2.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and BMI2 bit manipulation. The instance does not feature local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on networked Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent disk storage alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results characterize the entry-tier scale of the c5n.xlarge. In CPU-focused metrics, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1133.0 and a multi-core score of 2509.0, placing its raw compute throughput in the lower quartile of current cloud platforms. Stress-ng scores register at 1406.1 for single-core and 3689.06 for multi-core execution. Memory tests report large-block uncached read and write throughput of 25.89 GB/sec and 23.1 GB/sec, respectively, with PassMark memory scoring in the bottom decile at 1031.78. In workload testing, the instance managed 3.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.82 GB/sec static web throughput, while small 135M language model generation attained an average score of 75.07 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.xlarge functions as an entry-level compute node paired with higher network capability than standard c5 counterparts. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires careful management of remote EBS storage costs and latency. With its combination of dedicated Xeon cores, AVX-512 extensions, and moderate network throughput, this instance fits lightweight batch jobs, distributed build agents, continuous integration tasks, and intermediary network processing functions where massive RAM or multi-core parallelism is not required.
